name: Checkpoint128 visual and twenty-prediction evaluation: failed action controls
body:
# Checkpoint 128 evaluation: both requested action controls failed

The door remains closed throughout both 17-frame clips, and the requested 112.5-degree left camera turn is absent. Both clips retain a recognizable room and natural colors, with soft surfaces and small texture changes. All 34 frames were reviewed. The fixed original 947,712-parameter action adapter, native Wan foundation and VAE remained unchanged during evaluation. This is a failed command-control result on one seen room and one common sampling noise, not a validated controller.

Both branches use the same initial observation, saved noise and text; commands differ only at the first transition (wait/interact), followed by 15 identical left turns. Each clip has 17 frames at 1248×704, sampled with 50-step native UniPC/shift 5/CFG5. Complete parent time for BOTH clips is 398.633 seconds including loading, hashing and decoding. The GIF playback rate is a presentation setting, not generation speed. `wait.gif`, `interact.gif` and `matched-comparison.png` provide small previews; every native PNG and raw FP32 frame is in the full recovery.

The independent saved-artifact visual audit passed all source/input/checkpoint identities, all 825 foundation before/after values, both 50-state sequences and their exact observed prefixes, RGB-to-PNG mapping and recorded resource caps. Such numerical integrity does not establish command following.

## Paired RGB and twenty-prediction findings

All 17 frames per arm were compared with the original targets and the matched checkpoint 16 clips. Future mean absolute RGB error for checkpoint 128 is 0.1835971495 (wait) /0.1955583772 (interact), versus 0.1789626381 /0.1903559489 for simply repeating the starting image. Checkpoint 128 target error is slightly larger than checkpoint 16 by 0.0000465581 /0.0000354559. Both checkpoints score 0/16 on the strict both-branches-closer-to-own-truth test, including the paired-truth difference region. These correspondence measurements are sensitive to camera alignment and lighting; they are not a perceptual quality scale or a semantic door detector. Frame 0 is excluded from future averages. Targets retain exact original mapping and the declared LANCZOS resize/crop and canonical first-frame policy.

A separate 20-prediction diagnostic compared checkpoints 0,16,128 without training or image generation. At fixed k=506, checkpoint 128 future flow MSE is 0.147928055027 /0.161560970040 for closed/open examples, slightly above checkpoint 16 (0.147919876994 /0.161552561582). Both are slightly below initialization. On the shared initial k=999 input, the guided command RMS grows from 0.001961411819 at 16 to 0.004942172282 at 128, a 2.51970149× increase. Larger numerical sensitivity did not yield the requested rendered action. First-step CFG does not show near-total cancellation, and this does not diagnose the entire trajectory. Four checkpoint 0/native comparisons are bit-exact. Separately, all 14 repeated reference prediction files are byte-identical to the earlier diagnostic, with complete call identities matched; `original14-reproduction.json` records that check.

The first 20-prediction reader failed on an extra `allocated <= reserved` comparison of sequentially sampled counters. A narrow reader-only correction removed that unsupported instantaneous relation. All producer resource limits and nonnegative-field checks remain. The original reader/failure, correction, passed v2 audit and independent review are separate assets. No producer code, limits, metrics or tensor bytes changed.

## Complete evidence and disclosed privacy derivative

All 608 original recovery member names are retained, covering completed visual and 20-prediction runs, inputs, exact sources and preparation/review records. Public uncompressed bytes:927,969,112. The new gzip-level 1 stream is 785,123,769 bytes across 82 parts: the first 17 are 16,000,000 bytes each and the remaining 65 are at most 8,000,000 bytes each.

Public index SHA256: `8bc6a96e379c8b87841cf4b2e6079aa3c29e50f6af4ddf77871b7f77a295e6ad`.

Public stream SHA256: `624dce4bfd3d10f8ab30f99be73bcb4f83d01b667ed0a9ee4823129cce5222e5`.

Original index SHA256: `78283c76c83f3f091c143308c61d93cc190788eb34c39c849123164d521e498a`.

Exactly three copies of the prior 128-training audit replace only the private workspace prefix in the operational top-level `run` field with `[WORKSPACE]/`. All other 605 files are byte-identical, and all numerical/scientific identity fields remain unchanged. Original plans retain the original audit hash references; `public-derivation.json` maps each original/published audit copy explicitly. No failure or member is discarded. The original recovery remains untouched locally; `original-index.json` preserves its identity. Recompression changes the public stream identity. This is a disclosed public derivative, not the original compressed stream.

Download `fetch_artifacts.py` and `release-download.json`, then run:

```sh
python3 fetch_artifacts.py --metadata release-download.json --output /absolute/fresh-recovery
```

The unchanged downloader verifies HTTPS sizes/digests, all ordered parts, the gzip stream and every extracted file. It rejects unsafe paths, links, duplicate/unexpected members and existing destinations. TLS checks remain enabled. Its historical module description mentions fixed 16; the supplied pinned metadata selects this release. No provider account or model is needed. `local-recovery-verification.json` records the complete pre-upload recovery. Publication requires exact remote digests and sizes; a fresh public download is recorded in the repository compact bundle afterward.

Runs are `recovered/action-results/final128-visual-v1` and `recovered/action-results/comparison128-spatial-v1`. Final adapter identity is `ac1160b22531804c473746d2fb8ee9edd75710e0e43d6f1eabc86d268c864996`; its original training evidence is in release `wan22-action-fixed128-a100-v1`. Dependency source is commit `099eeae6268da852b0acb580258e4c168f900520` plus exact local work programs retained in this recovery. The release target commit is publication context.

Original Worldline code and adapter weights use Apache-2.0. External Wan source/model/VAE retain Apache-2.0 and NOTICE. Original procedural Atrium imagery/metadata use CC0. Licenses are separate assets. No external foundation checkpoint, installed environment, provider credential or account-lifecycle record is included. This result does not establish generalization, architecture novelty or frontier-model parity.

The first 17 completed 16 MB assets are preserved. After one bounded 16 MB attempt failed at part 017, only the absent tail was divided into 8 MB or smaller pieces. The earlier 50-part index, metadata and local verification remain separate historical assets. The public gzip stream and every member are unchanged by this transport repair.
